title: Principal Investigator(s) in Reproduction, Pregnancy and Developmental Biology - Toronto (City), Ontario (CA) job with Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute | 12863027
gist: The Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute (Sinai Health, University of Toronto-affiliated) is recruiting one or more independent Principal Investigators, at the Assistant/Associate Professor level starting September 2027, for new research programs in maternal-fetal health or reproductive/developmental biology, backed by competitive start-up packages and access to major genomics, imaging, and biobanking core facilities.

insights.claim: The Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute (LTRI) of Sinai Health, a University of Toronto-affiliated research centre in Toronto, is recruiting Full-Time Principal Investigator(s) at rank equivalent to Assistant or Associate Professor, with cross-appointment at the University of Toronto, anticipated start date September 1, 2027 or by mutual agreement, offering competitive start-up packages and salaries.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Signals institutional research investment by a major Canadian academic health center in reproductive, maternal-fetal, and developmental biology — worth watching as a data point on where new biomedical research capacity is being built.

insights.claim: The institute is seeking candidates in two topic areas: (i) Maternal-Fetal Health, covering placentation, pregnancy complications such as preeclampsia, preterm birth and gestational diabetes, and the developmental origins of health and disease; and (ii) Reproductive and Developmental Biology, covering early embryogenesis, lineage specification, morphogenesis, and stem cell dynamics.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Defines the specific scientific niches the institute is prioritizing for growth, useful for tracking which subfields of reproductive/developmental biology are attracting new academic investment.
insights.locator: We are seeking new colleagues who will develop innovative

insights.claim: Named research approaches of interest explicitly include large-scale multi-omic datasets (single-cell genomics and spatial transcriptomics), advanced live-cell or super-resolution imaging, computational modeling of developmental trajectories, and engineered in vitro models such as stem cell-based embryo models, organoids, or micro-physiological systems.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The explicit listing of stem cell-based embryo models and organoids as target methodologies signals continued academic momentum in these emerging modeling technologies, relevant to tracking talent and funding flows into synthetic embryology and organoid platforms.
insights.locator: Research approaches and methodologies across both areas

insights.claim: LTRI hosts several named core facilities relevant to the search, including the Network Biology Collaborative Centre, the Nikon Centre of Excellence, The Centre for Phenogenomics (a mouse-model facility), and the Nanoscale Biomedical Imaging Facility, plus access to the Frances Bloomberg Centre for Women's and Infants' Health at Mount Sinai Hospital, described as Canada's largest academic centre for reproductive, maternal, and newborn care, supporting over 7,000 births per year.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
entities: Frances Bloomberg Centre for Women's and Infants' Health
insights.so_what: The scale of clinical volume (7,000+ births/year) and core facility infrastructure indicates a well-resourced translational research environment, relevant context for assessing the institute's competitiveness in recruiting top reproductive-biology talent.
insights.quote: supports the over 7,000 births each year, with particular expertise in complex and high-risk pregnancies and assisted reproductive technologies
insights.locator: Of particular relevance to this search

insights.claim: LTRI also runs the Ontario Birth Study, the Research Centre for Women's and Infants' Health (RCWIH) BioBank, and leads the Healthy Life Trajectories Initiative (HeLTI), a major international research program testing preconception interventions to prevent chronic childhood diseases such as obesity and diabetes.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Existing longitudinal cohort and biobank infrastructure (Ontario Birth Study, RCWIH BioBank) is a differentiated data asset a new PI would inherit access to, relevant when assessing the institute's capacity for large-cohort reproductive/developmental research.
insights.locator: The Institute hosts the Ontario Birth Study
